entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 11
 
Ex 11:1-10. Death of the First-born Threatened.

1. the Lord said--rather, "had said unto Moses." It may be inferred, therefore, that he had been apprised that the crisis had now arrived, that the next plague would so effectually humble and alarm the mind of Pharaoh, that he would "thrust them out thence altogether"; and thus the word of Moses (Ex 10:29), must be regarded as a prediction.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv685"/><div sID="gen967" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv685"/><hi type="bold">7. against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue--</hi>No town or village in Egypt or in the East generally is free from the nuisance of dogs, who prowl about the streets and make the most hideous noise at any passers-by at night. What an emphatic significance does the knowledge of this circumstance give to this fact in the sacred record, that on the awful night that was coming, when the air should be rent with the piercing shrieks of mourners, so great and universal would be the panic inspired by the hand of God, that not a dog would move his tongue against the children of Israel! <div eID="gen967" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv686"/><div sID="gen968" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv686"/><hi type="bold">8. all these thy servants shall ... bow down themselves unto me--</hi>This would be the effect of the universal terror; the hearts of the proudest would be humbled and do reverential homage to God, in the person of His representative.<div eID="gen968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen969" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">went out ... in a great anger--</hi>Holy and righteous indignation at the duplicity, repeated falsehood, and hardened impenitence of the king; and this strong emotion was stirred in the bosom of Moses, not at the ill reception given to himself, but the dishonor done to God (<reference osisRef="Matt.19.8">Mt 19:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.4.26">Ep 4:26</reference>). <chapter eID="Exod.11"/>
entries.content_plain:
8. all these thy servants shall ... bow down themselves unto me--This would be the effect of the universal terror; the hearts of the proudest would be humbled and do reverential homage to God, in the person of His representative.
 
went out ... in a great anger--Holy and righteous indignation at the duplicity, repeated falsehood, and hardened impenitence of the king; and this strong emotion was stirred in the bosom of Moses, not at the ill reception given to himself, but the dishonor done to God (Mt 19:8; Ep 4:26).
